content.value_statement: Managing Microsoft Playwright Testing workspaces through ARM requires specific Azure SDK calls. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise .NET guidance for workspace, quota, and service URL workflows.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the Azure.ResourceManager.Playwright and Azure.Identity package requirements.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential setup and subscription resource access for .NET.
Shows create, get, list, update, and delete flows for Playwright workspaces.
Covers quota lookup and workspace name availability checks through ARM.
Connects workspace creation to the dataplane service URL used for test execution.
limitations: Requires valid Azure credentials and permissions for the target subscription and resource group.
Does not run Playwright tests or replace the separate test execution SDK.
Examples need review for region, naming, tagging, and organization policy requirements.
Azure SDK versions and service APIs may change after the skill source date.

use_cases.title: Provision a workspace
use_cases.description: Create a Microsoft Playwright Testing workspace with ARM and capture its service URL.

use_cases.title: Review workspace operations
use_cases.description: Find the SDK calls for listing, updating, deleting, and checking workspace availability.

use_cases.title: Plan quota-aware rollout
use_cases.description: Check subscription and workspace quotas before expanding cloud browser test capacity.

prompt_templates.title: Install the SDK
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new .NET project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the packages and Azure authentication setup needed to manage Microsoft Playwright Testing workspaces with .NET.

prompt_templates.title: Create a workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a Playwright Testing workspace in an existing Azure resource group and explain each required SDK step.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect existing resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through listing Playwright Testing workspaces, checking name availability, and reading quota information in .NET.

prompt_templates.title: Design automation safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe automation plan for creating, tagging, quota-checking, and deleting Playwright Testing workspaces through Azure Resource Manager.

output_examples.input: I need to set up a .NET project for Playwright Testing workspace management.
output_examples.output: A setup plan listing required packages, Azure credential options, subscription access, and the first workspace collection call.

output_examples.input: I want to create a workspace and pass its service URL to test execution.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step workflow that creates the workspace, waits for completion, reads the dataplane URI, and stores it for tests.

output_examples.input: I need to understand quota and cleanup operations before automation.
output_examples.output: A review checklist covering quota queries, name checks, update behavior, delete impact, and required Azure permissions.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and least-privilege Azure roles for workspace management tasks.
Confirm subscription, resource group, region, and naming policy before running create or delete operations.
Handle Azure RequestFailedException cases and long-running operation behavior explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode Azure client secrets, subscription identifiers, or tenant details in source files.
Do not use management-plane SDK examples as a substitute for the separate test execution SDK.
Do not automate workspace deletion without explicit approval and recovery expectations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with Azure Resource Manager workflows for Microsoft Playwright Testing workspaces in .NET.

faq.question: Can it run Playwright tests?
faq.answer: No. It covers management-plane workspace operations, not browser test execution.

faq.question: Which authentication approach does it describe?
faq.answer: It describes DefaultAzureCredential and optional Azure environment variables for service principal authentication.

faq.question: Does it include quota guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows subscription-level and workspace-level quota lookup concepts.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production automation?
faq.answer: It can support automation planning, but all examples need policy, permission, and error-handling review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
